theorem_title: A four-exponentials counterexample in transcendence degree one yields polynomials too small at a transcendental number
formal_statement:
namespace FourExp

theorem small_polynomials_of_counterexample :
    ∀ l₁₁ l₁₂ l₂₁ l₂₂ : ℂ,
      IsAlgebraic ℚ (Complex.exp l₁₁) → IsAlgebraic ℚ (Complex.exp l₁₂) →
      IsAlgebraic ℚ (Complex.exp l₂₁) → IsAlgebraic ℚ (Complex.exp l₂₂) →
      l₁₁ ≠ 0 → l₁₂ ≠ 0 → l₂₁ ≠ 0 → l₂₂ ≠ 0 →
      l₁₁ * l₂₂ = l₁₂ * l₂₁ →
      Algebra.trdeg ℚ ↥(Algebra.adjoin ℚ ({l₁₁, l₁₂, l₂₁, l₂₂} : Set ℂ)) ≤ 1 →
      ¬ (∃ a b : ℚ, ¬(a = 0 ∧ b = 0) ∧
          (a : ℂ) * l₁₁ + (b : ℂ) * l₂₁ = 0 ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₁₂ + (b : ℂ) * l₂₂ = 0) →
      ¬ (∃ a b : ℚ, ¬(a = 0 ∧ b = 0) ∧
          (a : ℂ) * l₁₁ + (b : ℂ) * l₁₂ = 0 ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₂₁ + (b : ℂ) * l₂₂ = 0) →
      ∃ ω : ℂ, Transcendental ℚ ω ∧
        ∃ σ₁ σ₂ : ℝ → ℝ, StrictMono σ₁ ∧ StrictMono σ₂ ∧
          Tendsto σ₁ atTop atTop ∧ Tendsto σ₂ atTop atTop ∧
          ∃ a₁ a₂ : ℝ, 1 ≤ a₁ ∧ 1 ≤ a₂ ∧
            (∀ x : ℝ, 0 < x → σ₂ x ≤ σ₁ x) ∧
            (∀ x : ℝ, 0 < x → σ₁ (x + 1) ≤ a₁ * σ₁ x) ∧
            (∀ x : ℝ, 0 < x → σ₂ (x + 1) ≤ a₂ * σ₂ x) ∧
            ∀ C : ℝ, ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ P : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ < N →
              P N ≠ 0 ∧
              (∀ i : ℕ, |((P N).coeff i : ℝ)| ≤ Real.exp (σ₁ N)) ∧
              ((P N).natDegree : ℝ) ≤ σ₂ N ∧
              ‖Polynomial.aeval ω (P N)‖ < Real.exp (-(C * σ₁ N * σ₂ N)) := by
  sorry

end FourExp
source: M. Waldschmidt, Solution du huitième problème de Schneider, J. Number Theory 5 (1973), 191–202, §III, Lemmas 4–7; with the zero estimate of M. Waldschmidt, Bull. Soc. Math. France 99 (1971), 285–304, §4, Lemma 3, in place of the hypotheses (iii)–(iv) of Gel'fond's lemma. See also W. D. Brownawell, J. Number Theory 6 (1974), 22–31.
